subject: Proposal: structured multi-year prepay and credit schedule (renewal)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Renewals Team <renewals@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: structured multi-year prepay and credit schedule (renewal)

Hi Tom / Renewals Team,

Thanks again for the candid conversation earlier this week. Based on your usage profile and desire to lock pricing for the next three years, attached is a structured prepay approach that balances Acme's budget profile with Redwood's ability to guarantee price protection. High level:

- Year 1: 40% prepay of estimated committed spend with a 20% term discount off list rate.
- Year 2: 30% prepay with a 15% discount and optional top-up window after Q2.
- Year 3: optional 20% prepay at a 10% discount (customer option to elect in prior 90 days).
- Carry-forward credits for any unused prepay within the same 12-month period; separate overage billing at standard usage rates.

I attached a schedule (Acme_MultiYear_Schedule_v3.xlsx) showing the ramped credit allocation and an example invoicing cadence. A few notes:
- We can cap annual overage exposure at +25% of committed tokens; anything above that would be billed at an agreed overage rate.
- If Acme prefers all-upfront prepay, we can increase the discount by 5 percentage points; otherwise the staged approach keeps cashflow predictable for you.
- We will include a standard revenue recognition addendum handled by Laura in finance.

If this looks directionally right, I can route a DocuSign with the schedule and updated SOW. Goal: lock pricing for 36 months without requiring Acme to fully prepay on day one.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Mid-Market
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: Acme_MultiYear_Schedule_v3.xlsx (xlsx)
Attachment: Redwood_Prepay_Terms_2027.pdf (pdf)

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: structured multi-year prepay and credit schedule (renewal)

Camila,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the thoughtful structure. A couple of points from our side:

1) Budget: our CFO is comfortable with Year 1 prepay but wants to limit our committed cash outlay in subsequent years unless we secure a stronger price guarantee.
2) Discount: 20% Y1 is attractive but we were hoping to see a floor of 18–20% across all three years if we commit to the staged prepay.
3) Audit/controls: we need clearer language around data residency and a short SOC2 evidence package before legal signs off.

Would you be open to: 35% Year 1 prepay at 20% discount, 35% Year 2 at 18%, Year 3 optional at 15% — and we sign a mutual SLA credit in case of major downtime? If you can send a revised schedule and a DocuSign link, I can get our procurement team to review.

- Tom
Renewals Manager, Acme Media
tom.alvarez@acme.com

Attachment: Acme_Budget_Notes_Q1.pdf (pdf)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Re: Proposal: structured multi-year prepay and credit schedule (renewal)

Vivek / Laura — forwarding Acme's counter. Key asks: stronger year-over-year floor (Tom proposes 20%/18%/15% style) and SOC2 evidence + SLA credit. Procurement can sign quickly if we tighten the price floor and include an SLA credit clause.

My suggested internal options:
A) Match budget: 35% Y1 @20%, 35% Y2 @18%, 20% Y3 @15% (opt-in) — provide SOC2 snapshot and 30-day SLA credit for P99 breaches.
B) Keep staged prepay as I proposed but offer a 5% one-time signing credit (applied in month 1) to get them over the line.

Laura — can you confirm revenue recognition implications for option A (partial prepay across years) and whether Finance can accept a 30-day SLA credit clause without other concessions?

Vivek — if we accept option A, what flexibility do we have on the upfront % split (can we move to 30/40 split to reduce Acme's immediate cash)?

Camila

Camila/Laura — reading Tom's counter I think option A is workable with a small tweak. Recommend the following compromise:

- Commitment: 36 months, staged prepay.
- Year 1: 35% prepay at 20% discount.
- Year 2: 30% prepay at 18% discount.
- Year 3: 20% prepay at 15% discount (customer option to elect in Q4 of Year 2).
- Signing credit: Redwood will apply a one-time service credit equal to 3% of Year 1 committed value if Acme signs the schedule within 14 days. This reduces their immediate cash burden while preserving our economics.
- SLA: include mutual SLA credit up to 10% of monthly invoice for P99 > target (standard carve-outs apply). Finance to sign-off on exact wording.

Laura — finance action: confirm how we book the Year 2/3 optional prepay and whether the 3% signing credit needs to be amortized or treated as a contra-revenue credit. Also confirm ability to provide a SOC2 snapshot and the minimal packaging for procurement.

If finance signs off, I'll approve sending a redlined schedule and DocuSign link.

Vivek
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

- SLA: mutual credit up to 10% of monthly invoice for qualifying P99 breaches (standard carve-outs; detailed language in SOW).

Attached: Acme_MultiYear_Schedule_v3.xlsx (updated with the compromise numbers) and Redwood_Prepay_Terms_2027.pdf (legal language).
